title: Death and the Afterlife in England, 1200-1750
description: Examines death and attitudes toward the afterlife and the supernatural from the late Middle Ages to the beginning of the modern era. Themes include the late-medieval ars moriendi and ghost stories; martyrdom of Protestants and Catholics under "Bloody Mary" and Elizabeth I; murder; attitudes toward providence and the supernatural; crime and public execution in 17th and 18th century London; the rise of "rational religion" and the "secularization of suicide".
notes: Credit will be granted for only one of HSTR 316A, HIST 328, HIST 328A.
recommendations: HSTR 220 or HSTR 312 recommended prior to HSTR 316A.
